title: Cohort Fidelity Binding and Runtime Operator Handbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This handbook defines the Cohort Fidelity Binding pattern: a runtime-first contract that ties request-level fidelity tiers (quality/cost tradeoffs) to kernel scheduling and execution behavior. It is intended for runtime operators, SREs, and runtime engineers who coordinate kernel selection, admission, and rollback across mixed-tenancy GPU pools.

Scope
-----
- Applies to the inference serving runtime and scheduler components (kernel mapper, admission-controller, cohort manager).
- Covers policy, observability, runbook procedures, benchmarking recommendations, and known failure modes.
- Not intended for model training pipelines or control plane-only features.

Why this exists
----------------
We observed production incidents where aggressive kernel choice and cross-tenant packing produced regressions in output fidelity (hallucination rate / quality) while improving token cost. Cohort Fidelity Binding formalizes the mapping so the scheduler can make safe, observable tradeoffs and platform teams can audit fidelity changes.

Key concepts
------------
- Fidelity tier: a labeled quality-cost bucket (e.g., high, standard, low).
- Cohort: a short-lived grouping of requests sharing affinity and fidelity constraints (per-customer/per-route/per-model variant).
- Binding: immutable policy applied on cohort creation that constrains kernel family, quantization profile, KV cache behavior, and prefetch hints.
- Degradation budget: a soft limit (percentage) of requests allowed to run at lower fidelity for cost/availability reasons.

Architecture & Dataflow (overview)
--------------------------------
1. API / Ingress annotates requests with requested_fidelity and route metadata.
2. Cohort Manager assigns a cohort id and materializes the binding (policy lookup + augmentation).
3. Admission controller evaluates cohort binding against current capacity and SLOs.
4. Kernel mapper selects a kernel candidate set that satisfies binding constraints.
5. Execution runtime enforces kernel selection and emits binding telemetry.

Scheduler Contract: required fields
----------------------------------
The scheduler must expose the following contract to the runtime:
- cohort_id (string)
- fidelity_tier (enum: high|standard|low)
- kernel_hint (string list)
- quant_profile (string)
- allow_degradation (bool)
- degradation_deadline_ms (integer; optional)

Example scheduler policy (declarative YAML snippet)
--------------------------------------------------
```yaml
policies:
  - name: enterprise-high-fidelity
    match:
      route_prefix: /v1/generate/enterprise
    binding:
      fidelity_tier: high
      kernel_hint: [cuda-fp16-opt, upward-attn-optim]
      quant_profile: none
      allow_degradation: false

  - name: burst-standard-economy
    match:
      tag: burstable
    binding:
      fidelity_tier: standard
      kernel_hint: [cuda-fp16, opportunistic-fusion-v2]
      quant_profile: q4_0
      allow_degradation: true
      degradation_deadline_ms: 250
```

Operational observability (metrics & traces)
-------------------------------------------
Required metrics (emitted per cohort and per request):
- runtime.cohort.count (counter, cohort lifecycle events)
- runtime.binding.applied (gauge, 1 when binding enforced)
- runtime.binding.kernel_candidates (histogram, candidate sizes)
- runtime.fidelity.fallback_rate (ratio of requests served at lower fidelity)
- runtime.fidelity.quality_regression_pct (derived; requires eval hooks)
- kernel.selection.latency_ms (p95/p99)
- request.kvcache.hit_ratio (per-cohort)
Recommended traces must include: cohort_id, kernel_hint, quant_profile, decision_path and any cost estimates used.

SLOs and thresholds (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
- Per-route p95 latency target: 120ms for high fidelity; 180ms for standard; 300ms for low.
- Maximum fallback_rate (daily rolling): 0.5% for high; 2.5% for standard; 10% for low.
- Quality regression alert: >0.3% increase in regression_pct over 24h baseline triggers P1 review.

Runbook: Fidelity-binding incident diagnosis (step-by-step)
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Detect: Alert fired for fidelity.quality_regression_pct or sudden spike in fallback_rate.
2. Triage: Open incident page and capture cohort_id(s) from alert.
3. Inspect binding: `redwoodctl runtime cohorts get <cohort_id>` — confirm fidelity_tier and kernel_hint.
4. Correlate kernels: query `runtime.kernel.selection` traces for the cohort to see which kernel variant was selected.
5. Compare with golden eval set: execute the prompt set against the original (previous) kernel variant in the sandbox to reproduce regression.
6. If regression reproduced: run rollback path (see Remediation). If not: escalate to research/ML for model behavior analysis.

Remediation actions (ordered)
---------------------------
1. Soft rollback: update cohort binding to prefer the previous kernel family (CLI):
   - `redwoodctl runtime binding update --cohort <id> --kernel_hint \"cuda-fp16-opt\" --force`
2. Block new cohorts using same binding: set policy to `allow_degradation: false` and throttle via admin flags.
3. Canary test: create a shadow cohort with `fidelity_tier: high` and replay 1% traffic to validate.
4. If kernel-level bug suspected: pin kernel version on affected nodes and open kernel-rollout ticket.
5. Postmortem and prevention: add targeted evals to the continuous harness and add a specific regression alert.

Example CLI snippets
--------------------
- List active cohorts: `redwoodctl runtime cohorts list --since 1h`
- Get cohort: `redwoodctl runtime cohorts get <cohort_id> --format yaml`
- Force binding update: `redwoodctl runtime binding update --cohort <cohort_id> --set quant_profile=q4_1`

Benchmarking protocol for fidelity changes
-----------------------------------------
1. Baseline capture: run 10k requests distribution-matched to production for both current kernel and proposed kernel. Capture latency, p95/p99, token costs, KV hit ratios, and quality metrics (BLEU / ROUGE / eval prompts pass-rate).
2. Statistical test: require p95 latency not worsen by more than 5% and quality pass-rate delta <= 0.2% (for high fidelity) before rollout.
3. Stress test: emulate mixed-tenancy packing at 75–125% of expected concurrency to validate eviction and preempt behaviors.
4. Shadow run: deploy for 24h with shadowing on 5% of traffic and automated regression gating.

Profiling playbook (when fidelity regressions are intermittent)
------------------------------------------------------------
- Stratified sampling: collect traces stratified by cohort_id, input_length_bucket, and token_entropy_bucket.
- Kernel microbenchmarks: run the microbenchmark harness with identical sequence lengths and kvcache warmness to isolate kernel variance.
- Repro harness: use deterministic seeds and model weights pinned to the version used in production; log full random seed and kernel launch config.
- Signal enrichment: correlate GPU SM util, PCIe latency, nvlink errors and kernel selection decisions.

Known issues and cautions
------------------------
| Issue | Symptom | Temporary mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| q4_0 small-batch quality variance | Occasional 0.2–0.5% model-quality drop on short inputs | Prefer q4_1 for short sequence cohorts; adjust prefetch policy | inference-runtime-team |
| kernel-v2 dispatch floor | Increased selection latency p99 during high churn | Increase kernel_mapper cache TTL to 30s | kernel-team |
| kvcache-staleness-after-eviction | Stale KV reads cause token misalignment in long chats | Force warmup-pass for long-lived cohorts; conservative eviction for high-fidelity | runtime-sre |

Rollout checklist for new fidelity bindings
-----------------------------------------
- [ ] Define binding YAML and unit tests
- [ ] Add cohort-level eval set and backfill baseline metrics
- [ ] Run synthetic benchmark at 1x/2x concurrency profiles
- [ ] Shadow 5% traffic for 24h with regression gating
- [ ] Coordinate with kernel team to schedule rollout window
- [ ] Monitor metrics for 48h and run manual spot-checks on failing prompts

Operational responsibilities and ownership matrix
------------------------------------------------
- Cohort Manager code/contract: runtime-core (owner)
- Scheduler policy validation and tooling: kernel-and-scheduling (owner)
- Quality/eval harness for cohort regressions: applied-ml-and-evals (owner)
- Incident remediation and rollout: eng-sre + runtime-core oncall (owners)

Appendix: example minimal binding JSON (for API)
------------------------------------------------
```json
{
  \"cohort_id\": \"c-20260112-abc123\",
  \"fidelity_tier\": \"standard\",
  \"kernel_hint\": [\"cuda-fp16\"],
  \"quant_profile\": \"q4_1\",
  \"allow_degradation\": true
}
```
